data.title: Match Preview | Austria v Republic of Ireland - Ireland target victory in Linz
data.content:
Team News  
   
 Heimir Hallgrímsson has confirmed that Seamus Coleman will not be involved in the match-day squad tomorrow night, though he has not ruled the defender out of Tuesday's fixture against Kosovo.  
 The Ireland Head Coach also has five players currently on yellow cards who risk suspension for the Aviva Stadium decider, but the squad has reported no fresh injury concerns ahead of the Austria clash.

Match Officials [...] - Austria have conceded 14 goals across their last eight matches, failing to keep a single clean sheet in that time. It’s more than they shipped in their previous 19 games combined (13).  
 - In 2026, the Republic of Ireland have scored 15 goals and conceded only seven, their best positive goal difference (+8) in any calendar year since 2021 (20 goals, 10 conceded, +10). As recently as 2024, Eire had a minus 12 goal difference (5 goals, 17 conceded). [...] - Austria are unbeaten in their last 16 home matches across all competitions (W13 D3) since losing 3-2 to Belgium in October 2023. They have scored 48 goals across those 16 games and never conceded more than once in a single game.  
 - Republic of Ireland have lost one of their last 12 games across all competitions (W6 D5), a 1-0 defeat away at Kosovo in September 2026 in the UEFA Nations League.

data.title: Republic to play home, away
data.content:
After the drama involved in playing Israel twice last month, we should have a quieter international window this weekend, with an away game against Austria on Saturday and a home game against Kosovo on Tuesday next, which will be the Republic of Ireland’s last game of 2026. When naming his squad for the two upcoming games, Irish coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said that Séamus Coleman will be involved with the Irish squad in these games in a hybrid player/coach role amid uncertainty over whether the [...] Everton goalkeeper Mark Travers, seen making a save for Ireland against Canada in Montréal last June, is back in the national squad for the games against Austria and Kosovo over the next few days. [Inpho/Ryan Byrne]

# Republic to play home, away

November 12, 2026 by Sean Creedon [...] Our game against Austria on Saturday will be played in Linz, a city in Northern Austria that will bring back bad memories for mature Irish fans like myself, who remember a 6-0 defeat there in a European Championship qualifier in October 1971. Fifty-five years ago, after he replaced Mick Meagan as Irish manager, Liam Tuohy was fed up with English-based players withdrawing from the Irish squad.
